Nevertheless, Orbán maintained close ties with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.Since the election, Hungarian authorities have launched fraud and corruption investigations into several members of Orbán’s former government. Photograph: CBS Photo Archive/CBS/Getty Images Star Trek Walter Koenig, actor best known as Chekov on Star Trek, dies aged 90 The actor appeared in the cult 1960s show as well as many of the films but also worked as a writer Adrian Horton Mon 26 Oct 2026 13.18 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Walter Koenig, the actor known for playing Pavel Chekov throughout the Star Trek franchise, has died, his representative confirmed to the Hollywood Reporter . He was 90. Koenig died at his home in North Hollywood surrounded by his daughter and niece, according to a Facebook post by Zachery McGinnis, the founder of Galactic Productions, an appearance agency that counted the actor as one of its clients. His death was attributed to “old age”, with no other details provided. “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world,” McGinnis wrote. “Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen. properties.article_text_excerpt: French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said that targeted curfews introduced in parts of Paris and other major cities “have contributed to calm overnight,” as he suggested more curfews could be introduced if needed today. In a particular symbol of stepped up security measures, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square, AFP said. While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days, the agency noted. Meanwhile, Italy’s government decided to dispatch 500 army troops to Milan after two days of unrest in the city, with shops in the city centre affected by riots and looting. properties.article_text_excerpt: President Nikos Christodoulides on Sunday reiterated his call for local authorities to suggest to the government “projects” to be undertaken using funds he said the Republic of Cyprus has “secured” as part of the European Union’s next multiannual financial framework, despite negotiations to devise that framework being far from over between the bloc’s 27 member states. “Our country has secured, through a combination of European funds and national financing, a total of €3.5 billion for projects across the Republic of Cyprus. The projects will be determined by cabinet in September 2027. You have ten months to bring these projects to maturity with the assistance of the district governments,” he said. He added that once those projects are approved by cabinet, they will begin to be implemented “immediately”, and said to this end that “it is, therefore, up to you to develop these projects and bring them forward to us”.
